chunks: One of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Habib al-Khash'ami, from Abu Sara, the prayer leader of the mosque of the Banu Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Today there is no one weak (of understanding); the men have delivered to the men, and the women to the women.

key_terms.الرِّجَالُ الرِّجَالَ: The men to the men (indicating men conveying the message to other men)
key_terms.النِّسَاءُ النِّسَاءَ: The women to the women (indicating women conveying the message to other women)
key_terms.مُسْتَضْعَفٌ: Weak (of understanding/faith), one who is easily misled or ignorant

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that there is no longer a 'weak' person in understanding?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that the era of the 'weak' (al-mustad'afun)—those excused from religious duties due to lack of knowledge or capacity—has passed, as the message has been fully conveyed to both men and women. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, signifies the completion of *tabligh* (propagation) and the onset of general accountability (*taklif*) for the entire community, marking a shift from selective guidance to universal obligation.

en.hubeali:
One of our companions, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Habeeb Al Khash’amy, from Abu Sara, the prayer leader of the Masjid of the Clan of Hilal, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Today there is no one weak (of understanding). The men have delivered (the Message) to the men, and the women to the women’.
en.sarwar: 12. Certain individuals of our people have narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Ali ibn Habib al-Khath’ami from abu Sarah Imam of the Mosque of Banu Hilal from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Today no one is a feeble-minded person. Men have informed men and women have informed women.”
